answer: Like a slow glacier grinding stone, decentralized consensus resists Sybil swarms through time-locked stake and proof-of-interaction. A solitary attacker cannot swiftly clone organic trust: minting identities requires rooting deep reputation like a resilient mountain juniper, while validating peers must strike with the verified accuracy of a hunting falcon. Because cross-verification difficulty scales superlinearly, synthetic node replication incurs exponential cost.
